label: Is ironman
summary: Whether the game rules are set to ironman mode, going by the name.
details: Vanilla texts do not use it on this type. The only lines with the same function name belong to the save window, so it is a hint, not proof. The game rules window has buttons that call SetIronman with yes or no.

label: Is preset window shown
summary: Whether the window for saving a game rules preset is currently open.
details: Vanilla uses it in the game rules screen, together with 'is host' and 'game not started for the first time', to decide whether a widget is visible.

label: Is valid preset name
summary: Whether the name typed for a new game rules preset can be used.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch the save-preset button on or off. When the name is not valid, the button's tooltip shows the text from GetInvalidPresetNameTooltip instead.

label: Preset name changed
summary: A GUI action that takes a preset name, going by the name to set the preset name field.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the game rules screen, passing the name of the clicked preset (GuiGameRulePreset.GetName). What it does with the name is read from the function's name only. It returns nothing.

label: Preset name edited
summary: A GUI action that runs while the player edits the preset name text box.
details: Vanilla attaches it to the text box's 'text edited' event in the game rules screen. It returns nothing.

label: Preset selected
summary: A GUI action that runs when the selection in a list changes, going by the name to pick a game rules preset.
details: Vanilla attaches it to a list's 'selection changed' event in the game rules screen. It returns nothing.

label: Reset rules to defaults
summary: A GUI action that, going by the name, sets all game rules back to their defaults.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the game rules screen. It returns nothing.

label: Save preset
summary: A GUI action that saves the current game rules as a preset.
details: Vanilla calls it from two button clicks in the game rules screen. It returns nothing.

label: Select category
summary: A GUI action that runs when the selection in a list changes, going by the name to pick a category of game rules.
details: Vanilla attaches it to a list's 'selection changed' event in the game rules screen. It returns nothing.

label: Game rules itself
summary: The game rules object itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The many lines with the same name belong to other types (for example a character's Self), so they only show that every type has a Self. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set ironman
summary: A GUI action that turns ironman mode on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from two buttons in the game rules screen, once with yes and once with no, written as '(bool)yes' and '(bool)no'. It returns nothing.

label: Set preset name
summary: A GUI action that applies the typed preset name when a button is clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the game rules screen. It takes no argument and returns nothing, so what it reads is not visible here.

label: Show preset window
summary: A GUI action that opens the window for saving a game rules preset.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the game rules screen. It returns nothing.

label: Notification itself
summary: Gives access to the notification object itself, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (a widget's AccessSelf), so they are only a hint. The game documents nothing more.

label: Accept button text
summary: The text on the notification's accept button.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a button in the message notification window.

label: Notification date
summary: The date of the notification, going by the name.
details: Vanilla texts do not use it on this type. Lines with the same name belong to save games and house unity entries, where it is followed by GetString. The game lists the return type as unregistered.

label: Date or time
summary: The date or time stamp of one of the engine's notifications, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it on the notification item in the engine's notification overlay, below its title and text. When it is a date and when a time stamp is not shown.

label: Decline button text
summary: The text on the notification's decline button.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a button in the message notification window.

label: Notification text
summary: The main text of the notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as the body text in the message notification window.

label: Notification timestamp
summary: The timestamp of the notification as text, going by the name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Notification title
summary: The title of the notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as the title text in the message notification window.

label: Has date
summary: Whether the notification has a date, going by the name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has accept action
summary: Whether the notification has something to run when it is accepted.
details: Vanilla combines it with HasOnDecline: widgets are visible when either one is true, and another set of widgets is visible when neither is. The buttons are probably among them.

label: Has decline action
summary: Whether the notification has something to run when it is declined.
details: Vanilla combines it with HasOnAccept: widgets are visible when either one is true, and another set of widgets is visible when neither is. The buttons are probably among them.

label: Accept notification
summary: A GUI action that accepts the notification.
details: Vanilla calls it from two button clicks in the message notification window. It returns nothing.

label: Decline notification
summary: A GUI action that declines the notification.
details: Vanilla calls it from two button clicks in the message notification window. It returns nothing.

label: Click notification
summary: Handles a click on one of the engine's notifications.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button that covers the whole notification item in the engine's notification overlay. What a click does is not shown.

label: Notification itself
summary: The notification object itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (for example a character's Self), so they only show that every type has a Self. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set up notification
summary: Prepares a notification item's widget and gives back a notification context for it.
details: It takes one value: vanilla passes the item's own widget (`PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`) and uses the result as the `datacontext` of the notification item in the engine's notification overlay. What the context holds is not documented.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.text: The widget of the notification item.

label: Overlay itself
summary: Gives access to the notification overlay object itself, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (a widget's AccessSelf), so they are only a hint. The game documents nothing more.

label: Alert count
summary: How many alerts the notification overlay holds, going by the name.
details: It returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Alerts
summary: The list of alerts in the engine's notification overlay.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list (`datamodel`) of notification items in the overlay, separate from the list of GetNotifications. How an alert differs from a notification is not shown. The game does not register its return type.

label: Notifications in category
summary: How many notifications are in a given category, going by the name.
details: It returns a whole number and takes one argument, probably the category. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the category to count, going by the name.

label: Notification count
summary: How many notifications the overlay holds, going by the name.
details: It returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Notifications
summary: The list of notifications in the engine's notification overlay.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list (`datamodel`) of notification items in the overlay, separate from the list of GetAlerts. The game does not register its return type.

label: Hide sidebar
summary: A GUI action that hides the overlay's sidebar, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Overlay itself
summary: The notification overlay object itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (for example a character's Self), so they only show that every type has a Self. The game documents nothing more.

label: Show sidebar
summary: A GUI action that shows the overlay's sidebar, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Toggle sidebar
summary: A GUI action that shows the overlay's sidebar if hidden and hides it if shown, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Password popup itself
summary: Gives access to the password popup object itself, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (a widget's AccessSelf), so they are only a hint. The game documents nothing more.

label: Cancel password
summary: A GUI action that cancels the password popup.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the multiplayer screens. It returns nothing.

label: Submit password
summary: A GUI action that sends in the typed password.
details: Vanilla calls it both when Return is pressed in the text box and when a button is clicked, in the multiplayer screens. It returns nothing.

label: Password popup itself
summary: The password popup object itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (for example a character's Self), so they only show that every type has a Self. The game documents nothing more.

label: Server itself
summary: Gives access to the multiplayer server entry itself, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (a widget's AccessSelf), so they are only a hint. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has password
summary: Whether the multiplayer server is protected by a password.
details: Vanilla uses it in the server list to decide whether a widget is visible, most likely a lock icon.

label: Max players
summary: The most players the multiplayer server allows.
details: Vanilla shows it after a slash, as 'players / max players', in the server list.

label: Server name
summary: The name of the multiplayer server.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a row in the server list. The very high count of uses of GetName comes from other types.

label: Number of players
summary: How many players are on the multiplayer server now.
details: Vanilla shows it before a slash, as 'players / max players', in the server list.

label: Server status
summary: The status of the multiplayer server as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a column in the server list.

label: Server version
summary: The game version the multiplayer server runs, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a column in the server list.

label: Is same version
summary: Whether the server runs the same game version as the player.
details: Vanilla uses it in the server list in two ways. A tooltip shows only when this is false, and a button (most likely the join button) is enabled only when it is true.

label: Join server
summary: A GUI action that joins the multiplayer server.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the server list. It returns nothing. The count of uses of the name Join includes other types.

label: Server itself
summary: The multiplayer server entry itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (for example a character's Self), so they only show that every type has a Self. The game documents nothing more.

label: Server browser itself
summary: Gives access to the server browser object itself, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (a widget's AccessSelf), so they are only a hint. The game documents nothing more.

label: Servers
summary: The list of multiplayer servers the browser knows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of the server list. It also checks whether this list is empty, together with IsRefreshing, to decide whether a widget is visible.

label: Servers (getter)
summary: The servers of the browser, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. Vanilla never uses it; it uses AccessServers instead.

label: Cross-platform filter on
summary: Whether the cross-platform filter of the server browser is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it, negated with Not, as the checked state of a check box in the browser's filters.

label: Empty filter on
summary: Whether the 'empty servers' filter is switched on, going by the name.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Full filter on
summary: Whether the 'full servers' filter is switched on, going by the name.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Password filter on
summary: Whether the filter on servers with a password is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it, negated with Not, as the checked state of a check box in the browser's filters.

label: Is refreshing
summary: Whether the server browser is just now reloading its server list.
details: Vanilla uses it with an 'is the list empty' check to show a widget while the list is empty or being refreshed.

label: Same mods filter on
summary: Whether the 'same mods' filter is switched on, going by the name.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Same version filter on
summary: Whether the same-version filter of the server browser is switched on, going by the name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a check box in the browser's filters. What the filter does is read from the name only.

label: Is sorted ascending
summary: Whether the server list is sorted in ascending order.
details: Vanilla combines it with IsSortedBy for a column ('name', 'players_count' and others) to show or hide a widget on that column, probably the sort arrow.

label: Is sorted by
summary: Whether the server list is currently sorted by the given column.
details: Vanilla passes a column name such as 'name' or 'players_count' and combines it with IsSortAscending to show or hide a widget, probably the sort arrow.

label: Join server by id
summary: A GUI action that joins a server by an id, going by the name.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the multiplayer screens. It takes no argument and returns nothing, so where the id comes from is not shown. SetServerId is probably what sets it.

label: Filter text edited
summary: A GUI action that runs while the player edits the filter text box.
details: Vanilla attaches it to the text box's 'text edited' event in the server browser. It returns nothing.

label: Refresh servers
summary: A GUI action that reloads the list of servers.
details: Vanilla calls it from two button clicks in the server browser. It returns nothing.

label: Server browser itself
summary: The server browser object itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (for example a character's Self), so they only show that every type has a Self. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set filter text
summary: A GUI action that sets the browser's filter text, going by the name.
details: It takes no argument and returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Set server id
summary: A GUI action that remembers which server is meant, going by the name.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the multiplayer screens. It takes no argument and returns nothing, so the exact source of the id is not visible. JoinServerWithId probably uses what is set here.

label: Sort servers
summary: A GUI action that sorts the server list by the given column.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks on column headers with 'name', 'players_count' or 'status'. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle cross-platform filter
summary: A GUI action that switches the cross-platform filter on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on a check box in the server browser. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle empty filter
summary: A GUI action that switches the 'empty servers' filter on or off, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Toggle full filter
summary: A GUI action that switches the 'full servers' filter on or off, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Toggle password filter
summary: A GUI action that switches the filter on servers with a password on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on a check box in the server browser. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle same mods filter
summary: A GUI action that switches the 'same mods' filter on or off, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Toggle same version filter
summary: A GUI action that switches the same-game-version filter on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on a check box in the server browser. It returns nothing.

label: Active page
summary: The settings page that is open now, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Settings pages
summary: The list of pages of the settings window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of a list in the settings window.

label: Settings window itself
summary: Gives access to the settings window object itself, going by the name.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (a widget's AccessSelf), so they are only a hint. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can apply
summary: Whether the settings window's Apply button can be used now.
details: Vanilla enables the 'Apply' button only when this is yes. When exactly that is (for example only after a change) is not shown.

label: Applied on restart
summary: Whether some of the changed settings only take effect after the game is restarted.
details: When it is yes, vanilla shows the 'restart required' mark and the text 'Some settings will not take effect until you restart the game.' at the bottom of the settings window.

label: Close settings
summary: Closes the settings window.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the window's 'x' button. Whether unapplied changes are kept or dropped is not shown.

label: Input action name
summary: The name of an input action (something a key can be bound to), as text.
details: It takes one value: vanilla passes a key binding (`InputActionBinding.Self`) and shows the result as the row's name on the controls page of the settings window.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.text: The key binding whose action is named.
fields.values: a key binding, as vanilla writes `InputActionBinding.Self`

label: Binding prompt
summary: The text of the 'Remap input' popup that asks for a new key for an action.
details: Vanilla shows it in the middle of the popup. The game's own text for it reads like 'Please choose an input binding for the action …', followed by the input chosen; that it is this text is read from the matching key `SETTINGS_INPUT_BINDING_TEXT`.

label: Input profile file
summary: The file name of the input profile (a saved set of key bindings), as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the editable field on the controls page of the settings window, next to 'Save Profile' and 'Load Profile'.

label: Bound key name
summary: The name of a key bound to an input action, as text.
details: It takes two values: vanilla passes a key binding (`InputActionBinding.Self`) and the number 0 or 1, and shows the two results as the action's two key buttons on the controls page. So each action has two binding slots.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.values: a key binding, as vanilla writes `InputActionBinding.Self`

fields.name: argument 2
fields.text: Which of the action's two keys.

label: Binding warning
summary: The warning shown in the 'Remap input' popup.
details: Vanilla shows it below the prompt only when ShouldShowWarningText is yes. The game's matching text `SETTINGS_INPUT_BINDING_WARNING_TEXT` warns that the binding already exists for another action and that confirming clears the old one; that this is the text is read from the key's name.

label: Has changed
summary: Whether the player has changed any setting that is not yet saved.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether a widget in the settings window is visible. That the changes are unsaved is read from the name.

label: Has default profile
summary: Whether a default input profile (the default key bindings) exists to reset to.
details: Vanilla enables the 'Reset to Defaults' button on the controls page only when this is yes.

label: Has profile file name
summary: Whether a file name for the input profile has been entered.
details: Vanilla enables the 'Save Profile' and 'Load Profile' buttons on the controls page only when this is yes.

label: Hide settings
summary: A GUI action that hides the settings window, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla texts do not use it on this type. The lines with the same name belong to other windows.

label: Is open page
summary: Whether the settings window's open page is the page with the given id.
details: It takes one text value. Vanilla checks `'settings_menu_controls'` to show the input profile buttons and field only on the controls page.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.text: The id of a settings page.
fields.values: a page id in quotes, such as `'settings_menu_controls'`

label: Input popup on
summary: Whether key bindings can be edited through the input popup.
details: Vanilla shows the rows of input actions with their key buttons on the controls page only when this is yes. When it is no is not shown.

label: Apply settings
summary: Applies the changed settings.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the settings window's 'Apply' button, which AllowApply enables.

label: Cancel remap
summary: Cancels the 'Remap input' popup without changing the key binding.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the popup's 'Cancel' button.

label: Clear binding
summary: Clears the key binding being edited in the 'Remap input' popup.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the popup's 'Clear' button.

label: Confirm binding
summary: Confirms the new key binding chosen in the 'Remap input' popup.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the popup's 'Confirm' button; the game's warning text says that confirming a key already bound to another action clears the old binding.

label: Reset key bindings
summary: Loads the default input profile, putting the key bindings back to their defaults.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Reset to Defaults' button on the controls page, which HasDefaultProfile enables.

label: Load input profile
summary: Loads the input profile (a saved set of key bindings) named in the file name field.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Load Profile' button on the controls page, which is enabled only when a file name is entered.

label: Save input profile
summary: Saves the current key bindings as an input profile under the name in the file name field.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Save Profile' button on the controls page, which is enabled only when a file name is entered.

label: Edit profile file name
summary: Takes the text typed into the input profile's file name field.
details: It returns nothing and takes no argument. Vanilla runs it whenever the text of that field on the controls page is edited.

label: Requires restart
summary: Whether the changed settings need a game restart to take effect.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether a widget in the settings window is visible, most likely a restart notice. One more use is commented out.

label: Restore settings
summary: A GUI action that restores the settings, probably to their earlier or default values.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the settings window. It returns nothing. Which values it restores is read from the name only.

label: Save settings
summary: A GUI action that saves the settings, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla texts do not use it on this type. The lines with the same name belong to saved games and event texts.

label: Save and close
summary: A GUI action that saves the settings and closes the settings window.
details: Vanilla calls it from three button clicks in the settings window. It returns nothing.

label: Settings window itself
summary: The settings window object itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
details: The game lists the return type as unregistered. The lines with the same name belong to other types (for example a character's Self), so they only show that every type has a Self. The game documents nothing more.

label: Show binding warning
summary: Whether the 'Remap input' popup shows its warning text.

label: Show settings
summary: A GUI action that shows the settings window, going by the name.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla texts do not use it on this type. The lines with the same name belong to other windows and texts.

label: Open remap popup
summary: Opens the 'Remap input' popup to choose a new key for one of an action's two bindings.
details: It returns nothing and takes three values. Vanilla runs it from an action's key buttons on the controls page, passing the input binding setting, the action's key binding and 0 or 1 for which of its two keys.

label: Lane right-click

summary: The keyframe editor object itself, so it can be passed on to something else.
